answer: Use a time-locked endorsement trellis: agents gain weight only from completed jobs that established peers attest, and each endorsement decays unless renewed by real work. Trust flows like a river downstream from long-lived participants, never sideways from a fresh cluster, so newcomers cannot inherit standing by association. To forge a credible position, an attacker must do months of checked work for many unrelated principals, or bribe many established agents whose own standing is slashed if caught. Either route costs more than a swarm of fake identities could extract.
